results.concept: The Broncos keep saying Bo Nix is on track for camp, but the next quarterback roster move will show whether they actually trust the ankle or are just trying to sound calm.

drafts.option1:
Broncos keep telling us Bo Nix is on track for camp. Cool.

The next QB they sign will tell you if they believe his ankle, or if they just believe in talking slow.
drafts.option2: When a team says the QB is on track, they mean on track to be on the injury report like everybody else. Watch the QB room, not the quotes. If they add another arm, that is ankle insurance.
drafts.option3:
Broncos fans are already practicing the calm voice. Bo is fine, everything is fine.

Then we carry an extra QB like it is a weather alert.

results.concept: The Nuggets say everything is on the table this summer, but nobody knows if that actually includes changing the non-Jokic minutes that keep wrecking games.

drafts.option1:
Nuggets keep saying everything is on the table this summer. Cool. But if the non Jokic minutes are still treated like a weather event, nothing changed.

We do not need more “options.” We need functional possessions.
drafts.option2:
Everything is on the table this summer. Except the one table we keep flipping every night, the Jokic rest minutes.

If the plan is still to just survive those possessions, congrats, that is the whole season again.
drafts.option3:
Nuggets fans all summer, just get us one more bench scorer and we are good. Then the game hits the non Jokic stretch and we start praying for a timeout like it is a substitute teacher.

Same movie, different month.

results.concept: The Avs are switching goalies after one loss even though the other goalie had been rolling.

drafts.option1:
Avs lose one game and we are already playing musical chairs in the crease. The other guy was rolling and now he is on the bench like he forgot his skates.

Nothing says confidence like a goalie hook after one L.
drafts.option2:
So the hot hand wins you games, until it loses you one. Then we act like the whole concept got solved overnight by the backup.

The crease is not a reset button.
drafts.option3:
We all do this thing where we say it is a long season, then demand a new goalie after one bad night. Patience lasts exactly one final horn.

Next up, changing lines every icing.

results.concept: The Rockies keep calling this a development year, but every road series turns into another reminder that the lineup cannot handle left-handed pitching.

drafts.option1:
Rockies keep calling it a development year, cool. Then we hit the road, see a lefty, and the lineup turns into a group project where nobody read the assignment. 

Next left handed starter is basically an off day.
drafts.option2:
Development year is fine. But if every road series becomes, can we please avoid the lefty, that is not development, that is a matchup allergy. 

The scouting report is one word. Left.
drafts.option3:
Rockies fans trying to stay positive like, it is a development year. Then a lefty starts on the road and we all remember the development is mostly learning how to strike out differently. 

Same pitcher, new coping.
